examples.en: The screen went blank without warning, which was disconcerting during the presentation.
examples.zh: 演示时，屏幕毫无预警地黑掉了，让人一下子有些慌乱。

examples.en: The shifting instructions were disconcerting the new volunteers.
examples.zh: 不断变化的指令让新来的志愿者们无所适从。

correction.currentProblem: The old adjective atom describes the affected person as 困惑的、不安的、尴尬的. The -ing adjective normally describes the thing or person causing a loss of ease, not merely feeling it. Its present-participle verb sense is valid and must remain represented.
validSensesToRetainAsOriginalComposition: An adjective describing a cause of disquiet, uncertainty or loss of composure.
The present participle of transitive disconcert: an action affecting another person.
excludedWrongEquivalences: disconcerting = a person merely feeling confused
disconcerting = a person merely feeling embarrassed
correction.activeRetentionProposal: Exclude the complete indivisible affected old tuple(s) from future active selected-sense alternatives only if independently approved; do not trim or relabel the third-party tuple. Keep the original canonical bytes, IDs and provenance unchanged.
scopeNotes: Do not remove the valid causative verb form to correct the adjective.
A person can be disconcerting if that person unsettles others; this does not turn the adjective into a description of that person feeling unsettled.
No general -ing/-ed rewrite rule or new word-family alias is proposed.
